sequence: M2DGR room_02, first 60 s of the raw bag

evaluation_protocol.alignment: rigid SE(3) fitted on the leading 20% of matched poses, never on the evaluation window

clean_lidar_inertial_only.note: img_en=0 control; isolates what the visual term contributes

lidar_only_88pct_near_field_occlusion_20.injection_scope: LiDAR stream only; the RGB stream is unchanged

findings: On this sequence FAST-LIVO2 is essentially immune to a LiDAR-only 88% near-field occlusion: ATE 0.0771 -> 0.0886 m (+15%), window RMSE 0.1077 -> 0.1287 m.

The visual term contributes nothing on the clean run (0.0771 m with vision vs 0.0761 m LiDAR-inertial only), so the invariance comes from the LiDAR-inertial solution surviving, not from vision rescuing it.

This does not reproduce the cross-modal contamination mechanism hypothesised for FAST-LIVO2 (contaminated VoxelMap depth corrupting the photometric term). A sequence where the LiDAR degenerates for longer, or where the camera is also degraded, is still needed before claiming either way.

M2DGR Mocap GT contains isolated corrupted samples: one at room_02 t=26.35 s moves 7.11 m and returns 20 ms later, which alone inflated ATE from 0.077 to 0.254 m and ATE_max to 7.05 m. The evaluator now rejects such samples and reports the count.
